questions.q: What does the Execute SQL Task at the start of the control flow do?
options: Truncates dbo.CapstoneFactOrderSales in AdventureWorksDW2014 before the load runs
Creates the AdventureWorks2012 database from scratch
Runs the entire data flow itself, without a separate Data Flow Task
Deletes the CapstoneDimProduct table permanently
questions.explain: This lesson's package does a full reload, so it truncates the fact table first, guarded by a success precedence constraint so the data flow never runs against a failed truncate.

questions.q: Why does the Lookup transformation have to run before the OLE DB Destination?
options: Because CapstoneFactOrderSales stores ProductKey, a surrogate key that only the Lookup can resolve from ProductID
Because SSIS requires every data flow to contain a Lookup transformation
Because the OLE DB Destination can't accept more than three columns without a Lookup first
It doesn't matter — the Lookup could just as easily run after the destination
questions.explain: There's no ProductKey to write until the Lookup matches the source's ProductID against CapstoneDimProduct and adds it to the pipeline.

questions.q: What does the Derived Column transformation compute in this package?
options: DateKey (in yyyymmdd integer format) and ExtendedAmount (OrderQty times UnitPrice)
The SalesOrderID and ProductID columns
A brand-new connection manager
The precedence constraint between the two control flow tasks
questions.explain: DateKey has to match DimDate's yyyymmdd integer format exactly to join correctly, and ExtendedAmount is a simple computed value the source query doesn't already provide in that shape.

questions.q: What query does the OLE DB Source run, and against which connection manager?
options: A join of Sales.SalesOrderHeader and Sales.SalesOrderDetail, against the AdventureWorks2012 connection manager
A SELECT against CapstoneFactOrderSales, against the AdventureWorksDW2014 connection manager
A stored procedure call with no parameters, against a flat file connection manager
It doesn't run a query — it reads directly from Production.Product only
questions.explain: The source pulls order header and order detail rows from AdventureWorks2012, joined on SalesOrderID, which is exactly the raw shape the rest of the data flow reshapes.

questions.q: After running the package twice in a row, what should the row count in dbo.CapstoneFactOrderSales look like?
options: The same both times — the truncate step means every run is a full reload, not an accumulation
Exactly double the first run's count
Zero, because truncate deletes the table structure itself
It's unpredictable and depends on network latency
questions.explain: Because the Execute SQL Task truncates the fact table before every load, re-running the package reloads the same data rather than duplicating it — that's the whole point of a full-load pattern.
